original.target_description: Study 1; national survey of psychologists; H6: norm of data sharing → intention toward adopting an open data badge; structural model estimated using PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 2.0).

n.sample_role: Psychologist survey respondents included in final data analysis of the PLS-SEM structural model
n.exclusions: 557 partial/full initial responses; responses with more than 10% missing values removed, leaving 397 valid responses; 56 respondents from disciplines other than psychology excluded, leaving 341.
n.location: p. 27, continuation of section 4.3, preceding section 4.4
n.quote: Therefore, a total of 341 responses from only psycholo- … gists were used for the final data analysis.

es.metric: β (PLS-SEM structural path coefficient; standardisation not explicitly stated)

replication.target_description: Xu and Zhang (2024), Study 1; Chinese communication scholars, final N=351; structural equation model standardized path coefficient: Subjective norms of data sharing → behavioral intentions toward data sharing. This is the conceptual replication counterpart identified by the supplied outcome and page locator.

n.location: p. 7, §4.3 Data Collection Procedure and Results
n.quote: This filtering resulted in the removal of 61 responses, leading to a final sample size of 351.
n.sample_role: Chinese communication scholars/respondents in final structural equation model sample
n.exclusions: 412 valid responses; excluded 20 completion times ≤361.3 seconds and 41 ≥1431 seconds; 61 removed; final 351.

notes:
Original primary-source acquisition failed; no original statistics taken from the replication paper. Replication uses Chinese communication scholars and data-sharing intentions rather than US psychologists and badge adoption. Reported success is the authors’ effect-specific narrative comparison, mapped to the supplied vocabulary.
Source follow-up: Fresh blind extraction from the named published article; title, authors and DOI verified on first page. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. Locator p. 6 corresponds to printed p. 28 (sixth PDF page). Printed coefficient is labelled β; no metric conversion was made. Internal source discrepancy: section 5.2 on p. 28 prints positive β = 0.201 and describes a positive influence, while Table 5 on p. 29 prints −.201*** for H6. Extraction retains the p. 28 narrative coefficient; discrepancy unresolved.
Completion source review (es_value_o): Named predictor and outcome identify this structural path. Extracted printed beta without conversion; standardisation is not explicitly stated. Table 5 prints −.201***; retained positive 0.201 from prose/Fig. 2 and recorded the discrepancy.
